MS-20261E-HB1.title: Appropriation; Department of Human Services to establish and implement youth diversion program.

actions.text: Motion to Reconsider Entered (Massengill, Read, Cockerham)

MS-20261E-HB1.description: AN ACT TO AMEND SECTION 22 OF CHAPTER 60, LAWS OF 2026, TO REVISE THE PURPOSE OF CERTAIN FUNDS APPROPRIATED TO THE DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN SERVICES FOR A YOUTH DIVERSION PROGRAM FOR FISCAL YEAR 2027; AND FOR RELATED PURPOSES.
MS-20261E-HB1.descriptionSource: Official summary (state legislature, via Open States)
MS-20261E-HB1.aiSummary: Mississippi lawmakers approved a change to how certain state funds for the Department of Human Services can be used for a youth diversion program in fiscal year 2027. The bill affects that department and the money set aside for this program. It was approved by the governor.

MS-20261E-SB2004.title: Department of Human Services; revise FY2027 appropriation to.
MS-20261E-SB2004.description: AN ACT TO AMEND SECTION 22 OF CHAPTER 60, LAWS OF 2026, TO REVISE THE PURPOSE OF CERTAIN FUNDS APPROPRIATED TO THE DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN SERVICES FOR A YOUTH DIVERSION PROGRAM FOR FISCAL YEAR 2027; AND FOR RELATED PURPOSES.
MS-20261E-SB2004.descriptionSource: Official summary (state legislature, via Open States)
MS-20261E-SB2004.aiSummary: The bill would revise how some fiscal year 2027 money for the Department of Human Services is used for a youth diversion program. It would change the purpose of those funds. It was referred to appropriations and later died on the calendar.

MS-2026-SR6.title: Urge U.S. Congress to enact legislation to include airguns and airbows as items taxed under the Pittman-Robertson Act.
MS-2026-SR6.description: A RESOLUTION URGING THE UNITED STATES CONGRESS TO ENACT LEGISLATION TO INCLUDE AIRGUNS AND AIRBOWS, WITH OTHER METHODS OF TAKE, AS ITEMS TAXED THROUGH THE FEDERAL WILDLIFE RESTORATION PROGRAM (PITTMAN-ROBERTSON ACT).
MS-2026-SR6.descriptionSource: Official summary (state legislature, via Open States)
MS-2026-SR6.aiSummary: The resolution would ask the U.S. Congress to pass a law that adds airguns and airbows to the items taxed under the federal Wildlife Restoration Program, also called the Pittman-Robertson Act. It would affect those products by placing them in the same tax program as other hunting items covered by that law.

MS-2026-SC533.title: Extend the sympathy of the Legislature to the family of national civil rights icon Reverend Jesse Jackson.
MS-2026-SC533.description: A CONCURRENT RESOLUTION EXTENDING THE SYMPATHY OF THE LEGISLATURE TO THE FAMILY OF NATIONAL CIVIL RIGHTS ICON REVEREND JESSE L. JACKSON, SR., ON HIS PASSING.
MS-2026-SC533.descriptionSource: Official summary (state legislature, via Open States)
MS-2026-SC533.aiSummary: This concurrent resolution would express the Mississippi Legislature’s sympathy to the family of Reverend Jesse L. Jackson, Sr. after his passing. It is a formal statement of support and condolence.

MS-2026-SB3108.title: City of Pass Christian; authorize municipal law enforcement to use one radar speed detection device on U.S. Highway 90.
MS-2026-SB3108.description: AN ACT TO AUTHORIZE THE CITY OF PASS CHRISTIAN, MISSISSIPPI, THROUGH ITS MUNICIPAL LAW ENFORCEMENT, TO OPERATE AND USE ONE RADAR SPEED DETECTION DEVICE TO ENFORCE THE MOTOR VEHICLE SPEED LIMITS ON THOSE PORTIONS OF U.S. HIGHWAY 90 THAT ARE LOCATED WITHIN THE CORPORATE LIMITS OF THE CITY; AND FOR RELATED PURPOSES.
MS-2026-SB3108.descriptionSource: Official summary (state legislature, via Open States)
MS-2026-SB3108.aiSummary: The bill would let Pass Christian city police use one radar speed device to check and enforce speed limits on parts of U.S. Highway 90 inside the city limits. It died in committee.

MS-2026-HB4175.description: AN ACT TO RESTORE THE RIGHT OF SUFFRAGE TO CHARLES COVINGTON OF LEE COUNTY, MISSISSIPPI.

MS-2026-HB4175.aiSummary: Would restore voting rights, called the right of suffrage, to Charles Covington of Lee County, Mississippi. It would apply to one named person only.

MS-2026-HB4100.title: DeSoto County; authorize sheriff to use radar on county roads.

actions.text: Referred To Local and Private Legislation

MS-2026-HB4100.description: AN ACT TO AUTHORIZE THE BOARD OF SUPERVISORS OF DESOTO COUNTY, MISSISSIPPI, TO PURCHASE RADAR SPEED DETECTION EQUIPMENT FOR USE BY THE SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT OF THE COUNTY IN THE ENFORCEMENT OF SPEED LIMITS ON THE ROADS AND STATE HIGHWAYS OF THE COUNTY OUTSIDE THE CORPORATE LIMITS OF ANY INCORPORATED MUNICIPALITY; TO PROVIDE THAT ANY FUNDS RECEIVED THROUGH USE OF SUCH EQUIPMENT SHALL BE USED TO FUND RESOURCE OFFICERS IN THE DESOTO COUNTY PUBLIC SCHOOLS; AND FOR RELATED PURPOSES.
MS-2026-HB4100.descriptionSource: Official summary (state legislature, via Open States)
MS-2026-HB4100.aiSummary: The measure would let the DeSoto County Board of Supervisors buy radar speed equipment for the sheriff’s department to help enforce speed limits on county roads and state highways outside city limits. Money from using that equipment would go to resource officers in DeSoto County public schools. It died in committee.
